name: session_recall
description: A realistic multi-session developer log for one service (payments/checkout/auth), plus queries written the way a developer asks weeks later. Entries were authored first, as a log; queries were authored afterwards without looking back at the entries' exact wording. See ../README.md for the authoring-bias disclosure.

entries.text: why does the checkout flow time out when the payment provider is slow?
The timeout comes from chargeCustomer in payments/gateway.ts -- it sets no explicit deadline, so it inherits the 30s default from the shared HTTP client. I gave it a 5s deadline and a bounded retry.

Decision: the payment gateway retries with exponential backoff and full jitter, capped at 3 attempts. More than that risks duplicate charges, because the provider is only idempotent above a 3 second window.
Added idempotencyKeyFor(order) so a retried attempt reuses the same key. Without it the third attempt could double-bill a customer.
where do we check that the session cookie is genuine?
validateSessionCookie in auth/session.go. It verifies the HMAC first, then the expiry. The comparison deliberately uses hmac.Equal rather than ==, so it runs in constant time.
Decision: refresh tokens rotate on every use. refreshUserAuthToken invalidates the previous token id, so a stolen one is single-use.
SessionStore has three implementations: Redis in production, an in-memory one for tests, and a Postgres one nobody has used since the migration.
the orders list page got noticeably worse this week
It is an N+1: fetchOrderLineItems runs inside the loop in renderOrdersTable. Batching it into a single query took p95 from 1.8s down to 220ms.
Measured on staging: orders list p95 1.8s -> 220ms after batching the line-item fetches into one round trip.
CI is red but only on one platform, what changed?
Windows CI failed because a test opened a generated markdown file without an explicit encoding, so it fell back to cp1252 and could not decode an em dash. Passing encoding='utf-8' fixed it.
Convention: always pass an explicit encoding to open() in tests. Windows runners default to cp1252 and will choke on any non-ASCII byte a generated file contains.
how are amounts stored, and why do the totals look off by a fraction?
All amounts are integer minor units in MoneyAmount -- never floats. formatMoney does the display conversion at the edge.
Decision: integer minor units everywhere. A float once crept into the refunds path and produced a one-unit drift that took two days to track down.
The generic helper in utils/retry.ts is shared -- the payment gateway is not its only caller, so changing its defaults affects the importer too.
add a regression test for the refunds bug
Added test_refund_rounds_to_minor_units, which pins the exact case that produced the drift.
The staging database is wiped every night at 02:00 UTC. Do not leave long-lived fixtures there expecting them to survive.
Renamed getUserById to findUserById so it matches the other repositories. Updated callers in six files.
walk me through how a change reaches production
Merges to main trigger GitHub Actions. Production has a manual approval gate on the deploy-prod environment; staging has none.
Rollback: deploy-prod keeps the last five releases. Trigger rollback.yml with the release id to go back; it takes about ninety seconds.
handleStripeWebhook verifies the signature before it parses the body. Order matters here -- do not move the JSON parse above the verification.
can the product catalog be cached, it barely changes
Added ProductCatalogCache, a 60 second in-process cache. Deliberately not Redis: the catalog is small and a one minute staleness budget is acceptable.
Open question: nobody on the team knows why LegacyOrderAdapter still exists. Ask the platform team before removing it.
OrderStateMachine permits pending to paid to shipped, and pending to cancelled. Going from paid to cancelled requires issuing a refund first.
why are there two settings files and which one wins
config.yaml is the checked-in default and config.local.yaml overrides it. loadConfig merges them, local last.
Gotcha: the local override file wins silently and is gitignored. If a setting appears to have no effect, look there before anywhere else.
Email goes through NotificationDispatcher. In tests it is swapped for a recorder, so nothing actually leaves the machine.
how long are we required to keep the audit trail
Audit events live in the audit_events table for 400 days, then a nightly job moves them to cold storage.
Compliance asked for 400 days specifically, not 365 -- it covers a full year plus the quarter-end review window that follows it.
parseCSVUpload rejects anything over 10MB. Larger files have to go through the asynchronous importer instead.
the ordering of results feels arbitrary to users
relevanceScore was never normalised by document length, so long descriptions dominated everything. Normalising it fixed the ordering.
